text:
maria: trying to cut a publish for the sampleapp JS SDK but CI failed on the typegen check. any quick ideas?
alex: saw the build. error was `type hash mismatch` during the check step.
maria: local `yarn typegen --check` shows expected vs found hashes. I haven't touched generated files.
jordan: often this is caused by nondeterministic ordering in the generator or a changelog tweak that changes the source input ordering. did the release branch get a later CHANGELOG edit?
sam: also confirm package.json version bumped correctly. npm publish will skip if same semver and cause confusing failures downstream.
maria: changelog was edited on main after branch cut. CI's regenerate step runs before publish and fails. locally, a regen produces a different hash than CI's check expects.
alex: could be the restore-cache step in CI pulling an old `types/` path, then the check compares stale file to regenerated one. we saw this cache race in a previous pipeline.
maria: build log snip:
```
build-bot: CI: failed job #4873 - typegen-verify
Error: hash mismatch for src/generated/openapi_types.ts
Expected: f0e1d2c3
Found: c3b2a190
```
jordan: short-term fix: push a regen commit that updates the generated file and increment patch semver, rerun publish. long-term: we should make the generator produce stable output (sort keys, stable iteration) and add a pre-merge hook to run `yarn typegen --check`.
sam: agree. also add CI step `typegen --regen --verify` that runs regen in a clean environment (no cache) so the check mirrors local runs.
maria: I'll push a regen + patch bump and include the exact `yarn typegen` invocation and node version in the commit message for traceability.
maria: pushed commit 3b7a9e (regen + v2.4.1 -> v2.4.2) at 1768543265
build-bot: CI: rerun job #4873 - typegen-verify -> passed
build-bot: CI: publish job started
alex: please open a tech-debt ticket to make generation deterministic and add a pre-merge check. this is burning time on releases.
maria: will do, linking to the CI job and including logs. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
